title: Policy Decision Point Contract
summary: Evaluate centrally auditable policy decisions and explanations without owning identity records or policy-authoring UI.

criteria: The evaluate(actor, action, resource, context) request shape and its party, capability and tenant inputs are human-approved before any implementation.
The Decision output is fixed as an allow|deny effect carrying reason, matchedPolicyId and traceId, with default-deny and deny-overrides semantics.
Hybrid RBAC, ABAC and ReBAC evaluation and system/platform/tenant layer resolution are specified as one deterministic model.
PEP enforcement/runtime, ECA/ruleset automation, identity record ownership and policy-authoring UI are explicit non-goals.

risks.desc: Missing, unknown or conflicting policy input could resolve to allow and silently widen access across the whole platform.
risks.mitigation: Require default-deny, priority plus deny-overrides resolution and missing/unknown/incomplete negative assertions before human-approved implementation.

risks.desc: Actor, resource or context mismatch could produce a decision that crosses tenant boundaries or leaks another tenant's policy.
risks.mitigation: Bind every request, decision and log record to one tenant and require Tenant A/B negative fixtures with redacted reasons.

risks.desc: A mutable or gap-prone decision log would destroy auditability and make permission simulation unverifiable.
risks.mitigation: Require append-only hash-chained decision log assertions, gap detection and named human approval for retention changes.

risks.desc: A planning decision contract could be misread as PEP enforcement, ECA automation, identity ownership or policy-authoring UI authority.
risks.mitigation: Keep exclusions and NO-GO explicit; reject implementation, readiness, release and deploy claims without new human authority.

featureDefs.title: Özellik Tanımları
items: evaluate(actor, action, resource, context) is the single typed entry point; the actor identity is taken as given and is never re-authenticated here.
The Decision is a deterministic allow|deny union carrying reason, matchedPolicyId and traceId so every answer is explainable.
Policy is data, not code: RBAC role rules, ABAC attribute rules and ReBAC relationship edges evaluate in one hybrid model with priority and deny-overrides.
Layer resolution runs system/platform/tenant in a fixed order, and permission simulation answers the same question as a side-effect-free dry-run.

PEP enforcement/runtime, ECA/ruleset automation, identity record ownership and policy-authoring UI are fixed non-goals: they stay outside this contract scope ve bu işlev sınırı insan onayı olmadan genişletilemez.
featureDefs.notes: policy-decision-point-contract/featureDefs: planning-only governance contract; no runtime evidence or readiness claim.
featureDefs.prompt: Policy Decision Point Contract featureDefs kapsamı. Kapsa: typed actor, action, resource and context request; allow|deny effect with reason, matchedPolicyId and traceId; hybrid RBAC, ABAC and ReBAC evaluation; default-deny, deny-overrides, system/platform/tenant layer resolution, tamper-evident decision log, permission simulation and explicit human approval. Exclude PEP enforcement/runtime, ECA/ruleset automation, identity record ownership and policy-authoring UI. Güvenlik sınırı: fixed exclusions and NO-GO cannot be relaxed. Çıktı: Produce planning evidence only.

security.title: Güvenlik Önlemleri
items: Tenant isolation is fail-closed: cross-tenant actor, resource or context mismatch returns default-deny with a redacted reason.
Conflicts resolve through explicit priority and deny-overrides; an absent, unknown or stale policy never becomes an implicit allow.
Human approval is required before any policy or decision behavior is implemented or activated; this node grants no apply authority.

codeOptimization.title: Kod Optimizasyonu
items: The planned handoff uses one versioned request type and one discriminated Decision type, with a short-code bütçe sınırı and katman separation instead of per-consumer permission checks.
Evaluation order, priority resolution and reason codes stay deterministic and testable; standard details are referenced through standardRefs instead of copied.
Decision cache keys, policy-version invalidation and batch evaluation are planned contracts only and claim no runtime implementation.

Least-privilege and deny-overrides remain invariant across the system/platform/tenant layers and cannot be relaxed by a lower layer.
Decision log records minimize and redact PII while retaining tenant, effect, reason, matchedPolicyId, traceId and policy-version evidence needed for review.

performance.title: Performans Optimizasyonu
items: The planned decision cache targets a cache-hit p95 of 5 ms or less and a cache-miss p95 of 25 ms or less; no measurement is claimed here.
Batch evaluation must use one data round trip and forbid N+1 policy or relationship lookups; cache keys include actor, action, resource, context hash and policy version.
Performance evidence must cover 100 to 100k policy scale, ReBAC graph depth limits and tenant-partitioned invalidation before any readiness claim.

Client surfaces may render reason-aware denied states only after a trusted backend decision; PEP enforcement/runtime remains a separate owner.

Automation may record a planned approval request but cannot bypass deny, change policy state or claim successful runtime execution.

testing.title: Testler & QA
items: Planned positive cases cover RBAC role, ABAC attribute and ReBAC relationship allow and deny decisions with exact reason, matchedPolicyId and traceId.
Planned negatives cover missing, unknown and incomplete context, cross-tenant mismatch, conflicting policies resolved by deny-overrides, stale policy version and spoofed context.
Permission simulation tests must prove the dry-run is side-effect free and returns the same effect as the evaluated path.

Contract tests must prove the tamper-evident decision log rejects mutation and gap, and that PEP enforcement/runtime, ECA/ruleset automation, identity record ownership and policy-authoring UI stay excluded.
The planned pytest command and kernelIntegration plannedTestRefs are future evidence requirements, not executed platform tests.

items: OWASP Broken Access Control risk is modeled through unknown permission, missing guard, cross-tenant resource access and client-supplied allow attempts; input validation is mandatory.
Every boundary validates tenant and context consistency and returns default-deny without leaking PII or policy internals in reason text.

Auditability requires an immutable hash-chained decision log with traceId, actor reference, tenant, action, resource reference, reason, matchedPolicyId and decision timestamps under retention controls.

observability.title: Gözlemlenebilirlik & Operasyon
items: Planned SLI/SLO and error-budget metrics include allow/deny/default-deny counts, cross-tenant rejects, reason-code distribution, simulation volume and evaluation latency by tenant-safe labels.
Logs and traces carry traceId, effect, reason, matchedPolicyId and policy version with PII redaction; high-cardinality actor/resource values are not metric labels.
Alerts cover any cross-tenant allow, default-allow regression, decision log gap or chain break and performance-budget breach; thresholds require human approval.

reliability.title: Dayanıklılık & Süreklilik
items: The primary failure mode is missing policy data, unknown fields, relationship-graph outage, stale cache or incomplete context; it degrades to deny and never to a default role or allow.
The same versioned request and policy snapshot must produce a deterministic decision; retry and idempotency controls cannot change decision log semantics or duplicate records.
Policy-version change invalidates cached decisions; rollback preserves deny behavior and decision log review without claiming a runtime mechanism exists.
